decision:
OVERTURN CONFIRMED: OPEN -> NARROWED.

Why the audit said OPEN. The audit graded OPEN for one reason only: no source could be read, because the alphaXiv quota was exhausted. It also set its own condition for a change: if the reads give about 768 mas for Proxima and 747-751 mas for alpha Cen AB, the grade becomes NARROWED.

What I read at source in this pass, independently of the verifiers:
- Kervella et al. 2016, arXiv:1610.06079v1.
  - p.1: AB at 'd = 1.338 +/- 0.001 pc (pi = 747.17 +/- 0.61 mas)'.
  - p.1: Proxima at 'pi = 768.13 +/- 1.04 mas; Lurie et al. 2014'.
  - p.1: alpha Centauri is called 'the triple star'.
  - Table 1, p.5: P16 743 +/- 1.3 mas against K16 747.17 +/- 0.61 mas; v_r = -22.3930 km/s.
  - Sec 5.3, p.12: alpha Cen's distance 'will not be measured accurately by the Gaia mission'.
- Pourbaix & Boffin 2016, arXiv:1601.01636.
  - p.2: 'revised orbital parallax (743 +/- 1.3 mas)'.
  - p.2: fitting or omitting Delta V_B changes the parallax by 2 %.
  - The paper rules out van Leeuwen 2007's 754.81 mas.
- Akeson et al. 2021, arXiv:2104.10086v2.
  - p.14: orbital parallax 750.81 +/- 0.38 mas, 0.49 % larger than K16; trigonometric parallax 747.1 +/- 5.2 mas.
  - Table 8: parallax rate +13.0 uas/yr.
  - p.9: Gaia standard processing is unavailable for AB.

Every condition the audit set for NARROWED is met at source.

Conversions, computed in this pass:
- AB: K16 4.3652 ly (+9.13 %), PB16 4.3897 ly (+9.74 %), A21 4.3441 ly (+8.60 %).
- Proxima, from Lurie as restated in K16: 4.2461 ly (+6.15 %).
- The 1 % price at AB is 2.787e10 to 2.817e10 Msun, which prints as 2.8e10. At Proxima it is 2.725e10, which prints as 2.7e10. phase1 prints 2.6e10 (phase1.py:552) and 2.57e10 (phase1.py:180).

I copied the three verifier scripts to adjudicate/run/ and re-ran them. All three report ALL PASS and exit 0.

Why NARROWED and not another grade:
- The measurement stands at source.
- The conclusions do not move under any value read. The price stays in the 1e10-Msun decade for L in [1.558, 15.58) ly, which keeps the 'galaxy of negative mass' sentence. Theorem 4's 3/2 does not depend on L (sympy).
- But the tree drops a hypothesis, the target. Figures computed for L = 4.0 ly are attached to the named 'Alpha Centauri' at phase1.py:182 and 552. Every READ distance is 6-10 % farther, so the printed prices hold only on the smaller class L = 4.0 ly. That is NARROWED.
- Not STANDS: the target is dropped, and the digits are 6-10 % low, in M's favour.
- Not WRONG: there is no computed contradiction. The printed digits are a discrepancy.
- Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the AB parallax has moved (743 -> 747.17 -> 750.81 mas, with PB16 and A21 in 5.77-sigma tension), but across that whole spread the price still prints 2.8e10 and stays in the same decade.

Did the verifiers share an error? I checked every READ value they quote against the pages returned to me: 747.17, 768.13, 743, 750.81, 747.1, v_r and the Gaia-brightness statements. All match. Their arithmetic also reproduces: the decade edges, the 5.77 sigma, the 5.8 % / 8.4 % framing, and the epoch drift. Akeson's +13.0 uas/yr gives 1.73e-5 per year, which independently confirms the 1.71e-5 per year the verifiers derived from v_r.

One limit they all share, and it does not change the grade: the Gaia DR3 Proxima parallax 768.0665 mas, which nonstatic.py:257 cites, is still NAMED-NOT-READ. Proxima is held only through restatements.
scope:
What the grade covers: the distance to 'Alpha Centauri' as phase1.py uses it. That means L = 4.0 ly, the 1 % and 50 % prices, L/2c and the amortised share. Those figures are correct arithmetic for L = 4.0 ly. For the named system they are 6-10 % low, whichever body is meant: AB at 4.344-4.390 ly (three READ orbital parallaxes) or Proxima at 4.246 ly. The order of magnitude and Theorem 4 are untouched.

What it does not cover:
- The physics behind establishment = L/2c, which is a separate key.
- The Gaia DR3 Proxima parallax of 768.0665 mas, which is NAMED-NOT-READ.
- Lurie 2014 itself, which was READ only as restated in K16.
- Which body phase1 meant. K16 calls alpha Centauri a triple, so the honest statement is a 6-10 % range, not one target.
corrections_to_record: Audit grade OPEN is superseded. Kervella 2016, Pourbaix & Boffin 2016 and Akeson 2021 were READ at source. Gaia DR3 768.0665 mas and Lurie 2014 stay NAMED-NOT-READ; Lurie is READ only as a restatement in K16 p.1.
Attribution settled at source: 747.17 +/- 0.61 mas is Kervella et al. 2016 (K16 p.1, Table 1). Pourbaix & Boffin 2016 give 743 +/- 1.3 mas.

The AB range is wider than the audit's '9.1-9.25 %' and '747-751 mas'. The READ orbital parallaxes run from 743 mas (+9.74 %, 4.3897 ly) to 750.81 mas (+8.60 %, 4.3441 ly). At every one of them the 1 % price prints 2.8e10 Msun (2.787e10 to 2.817e10) and the 50 % price 1.39e12 to 1.41e12.

lacked_data's '7e-5 relative' precision holds only for the unread Proxima DR3 figure. For AB, the READ parallaxes spread over 7.8 mas (about 1.05 %), PB16 against A21 is in 5.77-sigma tension, and PB16 names a 2 % model dependence on Delta V_B. The AB distance has moved at the 1-2 % level. That is evidence in kind for M's hypothesis, but 4-9x smaller than phase1's own rounding, and it moves no conclusion.

The epoch is now quantified. From the READ v_r = -22.393 km/s the distance changes by 1.71e-5 per year. Akeson 2021 Table 8 prints a parallax rate of +13.0 uas/yr, which is 1.73e-5 per year. Either way it is 0.17 % per century, which is negligible.
Percentage framing: +6.2 % and +9.1 % are measured relative to 4.0 ly. Relative to the true distance, 4.0 ly is short by 5.8 % (Proxima) and 8.4 % (K16 AB).

'WRONG would need a distance about ten times larger or smaller' is too loose. The 1 % price leaves the 1e10-Msun decade outside L in [1.558, 15.58) ly, a factor of about 2.6 down or 3.9 up. No READ value comes near either edge.
'Alpha Centauri, meaning the AB system' is an interpretation. K16 p.1 calls alpha Centauri 'the triple star', and phase1 names no body.

The printed digits are a discrepancy, not WRONG. phase1.py:180-181 print 2.57e10 and 1.28e12, and phase1.py:552 prints 2.6e10, all for L = 4.0 ly. At the named system the figures would be 2.7e10 to 2.8e10 and 1.36e12 to 1.41e12, so the device reads 6-10 % cheaper, in M's favour.
